sources_considered.why: Summarizes Graphite's measurement of the share of AI-generated articles over time.
Reports Graphite's finding that most articles shown in Google Search are human-written.
A search-quality study about affiliate SEO spam, not LLM content. Only its listing was found, and it was not read.

receipt.public_excerpt: Within the first 12 months, the percentage of primarily AI-generated articles jumped to 36%, and reached 48% by 24 months.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows a large rise in AI-generated web articles after ChatGPT. This supports the 'pumped our internet full' part, though not the cause or the quality effect.

receipt.public_excerpt: 86 percent of articles appearing in Google Search and 82 percent of those that appear on ChatGPT and Perplexity were written by people.

evidence_items.explanation: An October 2025 measurement, after the target period, suggesting that AI content mostly does not reach search users. That cuts against 'the information you look for is worse'.

unresolved_gaps: No study I found ties the quality of information found to OpenAI and Microsoft products in particular, or to these two leaders.
No measurement found of search-result quality before and after LLMs within the target period.
The Graphite figures rely on AI detectors, which have error rates.
